note.question: How does supplier learning shape the strategic role?
note.overview: This paper studies a procurement problem, where the supplier holds superior cost information and can learn to improve efficiency over time. Despite its prevalence, the supply chain literature provides limited guidance on how to manage learning suppliers with evolving private information.

models.name: The Strategic Role of Supplier Learning baseline model
models.summary: This paper studies a procurement problem, where the supplier holds superior cost information and can learn to improve efficiency over time. Despite its prevalence, the supply chain literature provides limited guidance on how to manage learning suppliers with evolving private information. The paper shows that supplier learning has both efficiency and agency effects, it can induce countervailing incentives, and the agency effect can overwhelm the efficiency effect.

source.quote: Problem definition: We study a procurement problem, where the supplier holds superior cost information and can learn to improve efficiency over time.
We show that supplier learning has both efficiency and agency effects, it can induce countervailing incentives, and the agency effect can overwhelm the efficiency effect.
A make-to-order supply chain has one buyer (she) and one supplier (he).

This insight has been ex­ tended to dynamic settings: In a regulation setting, Baron and Besanko (1984) show that the information rent is driven by precontract information only, that the rent size is determined by “informativeness measure” of the type, and that the principal can still fully extract the sur­ plus after the initial period.
Learning is fundamental to firm productivity and economic growth.
